question.problem:
Express ${\int }_{1}^{7}\frac{2}{x+3}\,\text{d}x$ as the limit of a left Riemann sum.

*Hint: Write down the missing expression in terms of $i$ and $n.$*

${\int }_{1}^{7}\frac{2}{x+3}\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[($
{{field-1}}
$)\cdot \frac{6}{n}]$
question.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{1}^{7}\frac{2}{x+3}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\frac{2}{x+3},$ the lower bound is $a=1,$ and the upper bound is $b=7.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{7-1}{n}=\frac{6}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{7}\frac{2}{x+3}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(1+i\cdot \frac{6}{n})\cdot \frac{6}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(1+\frac{6i}{n})\cdot \frac{6}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[\frac{2}{(1+6i/n)+3}\cdot \frac{6}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[(\frac{2}{6i/n+4})\cdot \frac{6}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[(\,\frac{1}{3i/n+2}\,)\cdot \frac{6}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
